name: Spot and escape a rip current
blurb: Rips cause the large majority of beach rescues, and they are usually visible from the shore if you know what to look for. This is fifteen minutes of learning that genuinely saves lives.
gear: A beach, ideally a lifeguarded one
steps: Learn to read one from the shore: a darker, calmer-looking gap in the breaking waves, often with churned sandy water and debris moving out.
Learn the counter-intuitive truth — the calm-looking patch is the dangerous one, not the choppy white water.
If caught: do not swim against it. A rip outruns an Olympic swimmer, and fighting it is what exhausts people.
Float or tread first to control your breathing, then swim parallel to the beach to exit the channel, then angle in with the waves.
Learn to signal for help: one arm raised and waved, and shout.
Practise spotting rips at several beaches and check your guess against the lifeguards.
tips: Swim between the flags where there are lifeguards. It is the single biggest risk reduction available.
If someone else is caught, do not swim out unaided — send help and throw something that floats. Rescuers drown too.
proof: You identify rips from the shore at an unfamiliar beach and a lifeguard confirms your reading.
